title: Field group
summary: A form drawn from a list of field specs: each entry becomes a pk-field with the right control (pk-input of every scalar type, pk-textarea, pk-select, pk-checkbox, pk-switch, pk-range, pk-combobox). Set fields (label, kind, hint, required, constraints, options, when) and values ({ key: value }); a committed change updates values and raises pk-field-change. A field with when (data: { field, equals | in | not }) or a visible(spec, values) callback property is not rendered at all while it is hidden, so a hidden required field can never block a submit; its value stays in values. A spec can also carry declarative conditions over the live committed values as text: whenExpr (or when given as a string), disabledExpr, readonlyExpr and requiredExpr, plus labelWhenExpr and helpWhenExpr for a label or help that follows the values, for example "status == 'paid' && amount > 100" (see the fields prop for the grammar); they are evaluated in the browser with no server round trip and no focus loss, by a module that loads only when a spec declares one. A combobox field takes its options from the search({ key, query }) callback property when it is set (a promise of [{ value, label }], like pk-combobox's pk-combo-query): the combobox then does not filter them itself, and a newer query makes an older answer stale. With a commit({ key, value, values }) callback property set, a committed change is handed to the host first and pk-field-change is raised only when it accepts: the field shows a busy state (aria-busy on the control and a small spinner beside the label) while the promise is pending, a newer edit of the same field supersedes an older pending one (last wins: a stale answer changes nothing and raises nothing), and a rejection or a returned string shows as that field's error message with the typed text kept. The controls live in this element's shadow tree. The element is form-associated: a surrounding form gets one FormData entry per shown field (a checkbox or switch only when checked; a hidden or disabled field none) and the first invalid field's message as its validity, anchored on that field, which is focused when a submit or reportValidity() fails; pk-form lists every problem through problems(), report() and checkField(). A form reset puts the values back to the ones last assigned.

props.name: fields
props.description: The field specs, in order: { key, label, kind?, hint?, help?, required?, whenExpr?, disabledExpr?, readonlyExpr?, requiredExpr?, labelWhenExpr?, helpWhenExpr?, readonly?, disabled?, hideLabel?, span?, placeholder?, min?, max?, step?, minlength?, maxlength?, pattern?, format?, decimals?, currency?, locale?, rows?, options?: [{ value, label }], free?, when?, msg? }. kind is text (default), number, email, password, date, time, url, tel, textarea, select, checkbox, switch, range or combobox, or custom (no control: the field's body is the child with slot editor-<key>; it has no value and takes no part in the form or its validation). hint is the line under the field, help a tooltip beside the label, span makes the field fill the row, format is money on an input kind (with decimals, currency, locale: pk-input's money format, the value stays the plain number), msg is { constraint: text } for the form's validation messages. Conditions: whenExpr (visible while true; `when` as a string is the same), disabledExpr, readonlyExpr and requiredExpr are expressions over the other fields' committed values: field keys, 'text' or "text" and number and true/false literals, == != < <= > >=, `key in [a, b]`, ! && || and parentheses; a bare key is true when it is not empty, false or 0; == compares as text unless both sides are numbers. There are no function calls or member access, nothing is evaluated as code. labelWhenExpr and helpWhenExpr are conditional text for the label and the help tooltip: `cond ? 'text' : cond ? 'text' : other`, where a value is a 'text' or another field's key (that field's value), for example "status == 'paid' ? 'Paid on' : due"; the first true condition wins, and an empty answer keeps label or help. A key that is not another field, or a syntax error, is warned once and reads as true for whenExpr, false for the other conditions and keeps the plain label or help for the text ones.

props.name: values
props.description: The current values, { key: value }: a string, a boolean (checkbox, switch) or a number (range). The element keeps its own copy and replaces this property when the user commits a change (it never edits the object you gave it); pk-field-change carries the same values.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name of the group. See prefix.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Submit each field as name.key instead of key (a form with two groups that use the same keys).

props.name: columns
props.description: How many columns the fields flow into; a field with span fills the row.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every control; also set by a disabled fieldset.

slots.description: Holds children whose slot is label-action- followed by a field key: each appears beside that field's label (a button, a badge). A child with no such slot name is not shown.

slots.name: editor-<key>
slots.description: The body of the custom field with that key: your own content in place of a control. It has no value and takes no part in the form or its validation.

events.name: pk-field-change
events.description: The user committed a change to one field: its key and value, and a fresh copy of every value. Fields whose when depends on it have already been shown or hidden.

parts.name: group
parts.description: The grid that holds the fields.

writes.target: the pk-field elements it builds in its own shadow tree
writes.why: requiredExpr, report(), checkField() and a form reset show or clear each field's message on the pk-field this element created and owns in its own shadow tree (never a host-given node); the fields are rebuilt from fields and values and removed with the element.

a11y: The host is role=group with the label as its name. Each field is a pk-field: a visible label, the hint under it and the error in its own region; the label, description and invalid state reach the control as properties, so nothing depends on an id crossing a shadow root. A field whose label is hidden (hideLabel) keeps it as the control's aria-label. A hidden field is removed from the tree, not just visually hidden.

examples.title: Fields with a conditional one (set fields and values from script: an inline script cannot run under this site's CSP)
Declarative conditions: Paid on shows while the status is paid, the reference is required above 100 and disabled when void, the memo is read-only once paid (no server round trip)
Conditional text: the label and the help tooltip follow the status (labelWhenExpr, helpWhenExpr)
examples.html: <pk-field-group label="Invoice" fields='[{"key":"status","label":"Status","kind":"select","options":[{"value":"open","label":"Open"},{"value":"paid","label":"Paid"}]},{"key":"due","label":"Due date","kind":"date","labelWhenExpr":"status == \u0027paid\u0027 ? \u0027Paid on\u0027 : \u0027Due on\u0027","helpWhenExpr":"status == \u0027paid\u0027 ? \u0027The day the money arrived.\u0027 : \u0027The day payment is expected.\u0027"}]' values='{"status":"open"}'></pk-field-group>

examples.title: A custom field: your own content in the field body (slot editor-<key>), no value and no part in the form

methods.name: problems()
methods.description: Every invalid shown field, in order: [{ key, label, message, control, focus() }]. pk-form lists these in its summary and focuses the first.

methods.name: report(on = true)
methods.description: Shows each invalid field's message in its pk-field (on), or clears every message (off).

methods.name: checkField(keyOrNode)
methods.description: Re-checks one field, showing or clearing its message; returns whether it is valid. pk-form uses it for live checks.

methods.name: snapshot()
methods.description: The values as the controls hold them now, { key: value }: what the user has typed even before it committed, with the committed value for a field that is not shown.

methods.name: setError(key, message)
methods.description: Shows a message in one field, for an answer from the server; an empty message clears it, and report(false) clears every message.

methods.name: focus()
methods.description: Focuses the first invalid field, else the first field.

methods.name: refresh()
methods.description: Draws the fields again; call it after changing the visible(spec, values) callback property.
